summary: Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and earned his PhD at McGill University (attested 2010), studying under G. Victor Sōgen Hori, Richard P. Hayes, and Palden Sherab, among others.

Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (1811–1894) was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Eugène Burnouf in 1838. He held professorships at INALCO, the Collège de France (1857, 1870–1894), and the University of Paris (circa 1862–1894).
Phillip Bloom is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Phra Brahmapundit (born 1955) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He has served as Chief Abbot at Wat Prayurawongsawat (circa 1996), Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (circa 1997–2018), and President of the International Association of Buddhist Universities (circa 2007).
Phra Khantipalo (1932–2021) was an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Jianmin Chen and served as abbot at Wat Buddha Dhamma beginning in 1978.
Phra Maha Singhathon Narasabho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University under the supervision of Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.

Phra Medhidhammaporn (born 1955) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Delhi by 1985 under the supervision of Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

Phra Rajavaramuni is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University, and served as Dean of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2012).

Phra Sigambhirayan specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Bachelor of Liberal Arts from Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phramaha Somphong Santacitto specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a master's degree in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).
Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Sydney under the supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle (attested 2009).

Phuntsok Tashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a BA from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, an MA from the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff (born 1947) is an Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from Harvard University (circa 1969–1973). She held professorships at McMaster University (circa 1976–2004) and Yale University (2004).

Pierre Bourdieu (1930–2002) was a philosopher who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1951) and under Émile Benveniste (circa 1951–1954). He held posts at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, EHESS (1975), and the Collège de France (1981–2001).

Pierre Chantraine (1899–1974) was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes between circa 1920 and 1927. He later held a post at the University of Paris from circa 1938 to 1969.

Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat (1936–2024) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held posts at EFEO and the French Institute of Pondicherry (1963–1967), the Chair of Sanskrit at EPHE (1967–2004), and served as President of the AIBL (2010).
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen specializes in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Leiden University by 1991, where he also served as a research fellow (attested 1996).

Pieter Hendrik Pott (1918–1989) worked in Indology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He served as a curator at Museum Volkenkunde (circa 1947–1965) and held a post at Leiden University (1973).

Pietro Merlo (1850–1888) studied linguistics and Indology at the University of Turin (1867) under Giovanni Flechia and Giovanni Maria Bertini. He taught at the University of Pavia from 1877, becoming full professor of comparative linguistics in 1885.

Piotr Balcerowicz (born 1964) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the Universities of Warsaw and Hamburg. He served as professor of Indology at the University of Warsaw (2011) and professor of international relations at SWPS University (2008–2011).
